text: Confirmed: `Interval.fromISO` parses both halves with `DateTime.fromISO` first, and when one half is a duration string that call returns an invalid DateTime — which, with `throwOnInvalid = true`, throws instead of falling back to `Duration.fromISO`. I'm applying the fix (tolerate the DateTime parse failure for each half, then fall back to duration parsing) and running the full test suite to make sure nothing regresses. ETA ~8 min.

Bug #2 confirmed and diagnosed: `objToLocalTS` (src/impl/util.js) feeds years 0–99 through `Date.UTC`, which interprets them as 19xx; the existing workaround only rewrites the year afterwards, so an un-normalized day (e.g. day 92 = Dec 31 + 61) gets normalized by JS using year 1999/2000 — and 2000 is a leap year while 100 is not, giving 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Fix: re-apply year/month/day together via `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`. Both fixes (#1 interval.js, #2 util.js) are being applied and verified against the full suite now; ETA ~10 min for both.

Bug #1 fixed and verified. `Interval.fromISO` now parses each half defensively: if `DateTime.fromISO` throws (which it does for a duration half when `throwOnInvalid = true`), that half is treated as "not a DateTime" and the code falls back to `Duration.fromISO` for the date+duration and duration+date forms. Both `"2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M"` and `"PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00"` now return the same valid Interval as with `throwOnInvalid` off (checked by equality against the default-settings result), the zone-argument and `P1Y2M10DT2H30M` cases still work, and genuinely unparsable input still throws `InvalidIntervalError` as documented. Full suite: 892 passed, same 2 failures as before my change (both pre-existing, in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js, caused by the container's ICU rendering the French hour without a leading zero — unrelated to this bug). Only src/interval.js was touched.

Bug #3 diagnosed: `isInDST` only compares the current offset against the offsets in January and May of the same year, so a year whose DST starts in January (1974) is misjudged. I'm collecting the exact per-month offset profile for 1974 (and southern-hemisphere zones) to pick a fix that doesn't regress normal years, then applying and verifying it. ETA ~12 min.

Bug #2 fixed and verified. `objToLocalTS` (src/impl/util.js) now re-applies year, month and day together via `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of only rewriting the year, so day-overflow arithmetic for years 0–99 is normalized with the correct leap-year rule (year 100 is not a leap year, 2000 is). `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 }).toISODate()` is now "0100-03-02"; +2 days → 0100-01-02, 0100-01-02 minus 2 days → 0099-12-31, 0099-12-31 + 60 days → 0100-03-01, 0096-12-31 + 61 days → 0097-03-02, and 0001-01-01 in UTC is unchanged. Full suite: 892 passed with only the same 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures (verified identical with the fix reverted). Only src/impl/util.js was touched.

Bug #4 fixed and verified. The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing `quarters` under `years` (casual and accurate) and `seconds` under `quarters` (casual), so `convert()` divided by `undefined` and produced NaN. Added `quarters: 4` to both `years` entries and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to casual `quarters`. Now `{ years: 1, quarters: 2 }.normalize()` → `{ years: 1, quarters: 2 }` and `{ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }.normalize()` → `{ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }`; `{ years: 1 }.shiftTo("quarters")` → `{ quarters: 4 }`, `{ quarters: 1 }.as("seconds")` → 7862400. An exhaustive sweep over all unit pairs × both conversion matrices × normalize/shiftTo/as found 0 remaining NaN (and the same sweep flags 48 failures with the fix reverted). test/duration: 114/114 pass; full suite unchanged apart from the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

Bug #3 fixed (src/datetime.js `isInDST` now probes January at day 1, so a year whose DST starts in January isn't mistaken for standard time). Verified: 1974-01-06T12:00 and 1974-06-08T12:00 in America/Los_Angeles now report true (both were false before), 1974-01-05T12:00 / 1974-10-27T12:00 / 1974-12-01 stay false, 1973/1975/1982/2020 and Australia/Sydney are unchanged, and a 1970–2030 sweep over both hemispheres shows 0 mismatches against the raw zone offsets. Note on your exact snippet: `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06")` is midnight local, and DST that year began at 02:00 local on Jan 6, so that instant is genuinely PST (isInDST false) — the same as in 1982/2020; noon on Jan 6 is now correctly true. test/datetime/zone.test.js: 30/30 pass.

Bug #5 (negative-year ISO padding) and #6 (FixedOffsetZone accepting a non-numeric offset) are being applied and verified now; ETA ~3 min for both.

Bug #6 fixed and verified. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js returned a hard-coded `true`; it now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so a zone built from a non-numeric offset reports itself invalid and any DateTime using it becomes invalid with reason "unsupported zone" (via the existing `!zone.isValid` check in the DateTime constructor). Verified: `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid` → false; `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone })` → isValid false, invalidReason "unsupported zone"; `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60)`/`utcInstance`/`instance(-300)`/`parseSpecifier("UTC+6")` and string specifiers like "UTC+7" all still valid, and `setZone("America/Blorp")` still gives "unsupported zone". test/zones + test/info + test/datetime/zone + test/datetime/create: 188/188 pass; full suite unchanged apart from the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

Bug #5 fixed. `padStart` in src/impl/util.js counted the minus sign as a digit, so `("00" + -1).slice(-2)` gave "00" for the year and the sign ended up in the middle. It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign: `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -1, month: 1, day: 1, zone: "utc" }).toISODate()` → "-0001-01-01", `{ year: -10 }` → "-0010-01-01", `{ year: -118040 }` → "-118040-05-25", while positive years ("1982-05-25", "+118040-05-25") and all offset/time padding are unchanged (offset formatting still goes through the same helper with non-negative values). test/datetime/format.test.js and the full suite show no new failures — only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat ones.
